summary: North Macedonia grants 90 visa-free days to citizens of the EU, UK, US, most of the Americas and its Balkan neighbors, while visa-required nationalities can either apply at an embassy or enter for up to 15 days per visit on a valid multiple-entry Schengen visa, an EU residence permit or (through 2026) a multiple-entry US, UK or Canadian visa.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for North Macedonia?
faq.answer: Most Western travelers don't: citizens of the EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia, Japan and most of the Americas can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period visa-free. Nationalities that need a visa can apply at a North Macedonian embassy, or enter for up to 15 days per visit if they hold a valid multiple-entry Schengen visa or EU residence permit, or, under a decision in force through 31 December 2026, a valid multiple-entry US, UK or Canadian visa.

faq.question: Can I enter North Macedonia with a Schengen visa?
faq.answer: Yes — holders of a valid multiple-entry Schengen (type C) visa can enter without a North Macedonian visa and stay up to 15 days per visit, provided the Schengen visa remains valid at least five days beyond the stay.

faq.question: How long can US citizens stay in North Macedonia?
faq.answer: US passport holders can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period without a visa.

faq.question: What currency is used in North Macedonia?
faq.answer: The Macedonian denar (MKD). Canada's travel advice says the economy is mostly cash-based, with credit cards accepted in some larger establishments and ATMs in urban centres. Australia's Smartraveller says the denar cannot be changed outside North Macedonia.

faq.question: Can EU citizens enter North Macedonia with just an ID card?
faq.answer: Yes. The Foreign Ministry says nationals of EU member states and Schengen signatories do not need a visa and may enter with a valid national identity card.
